reason: The section states one duty to establish a fund for a municipality with a generation facility.

evidenceText: shall establish a generation facility fund

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single fund-establishment requirement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipality constructing, owning, or operating a generation facility must establish a generation facility fund.

reason: Section 111.4 separates generation facility budget submission and balance rules from surplus and deficit handling.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Generation facility budget submission and balance
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address annual budget submission, balanced budgets, and charges against other operating funds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the budget submission, annual or quadrennial balance, and operating-fund charge rules for municipal generation facilities.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Generation facility surplus and deficit handling
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address debiting deficits, crediting or spreading surpluses, and transferring audited surplus.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how generation facility deficits and surpluses are applied, spread, or transferred to other municipal operating funds.

reason: The section is a focused reserve-fund power for generation facility ownership or operation.

evidenceText: with respect to its ownership or operation of a generation facility

proposedGroups.reason: The target authorizes reserve funds for generation facilities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipality may establish, manage, and contribute to operating and capital reserve funds for a generation facility.

reason: The section covers temporary borrowing for generation facility operation and a section 89 borrowing exclusion.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address borrowing for generation facilities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the temporary borrowing limit for generation facility operation and how construction or renovation borrowing is treated for section 89.

reason: This target only applies the generation-facility provisions in sections 111.1 to 111.6 to rural communities.
The section lists municipal powers when authorized to make a licensing by-law.

evidenceText: Where a municipality is authorized to make a by-law providing for licensing, it may

proposedGroups.reason: The target lists prohibitions, fees, terms, duration, renewal, suspension, revocation, delegation, and information requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipal powers available in licensing by-laws, including prohibitions, fees, terms, duration, renewal, suspension, revocation, delegation, and information requirements.

reason: The section is a focused scope rule for business licensing by-laws.

evidenceText: applies to a person whether or not

proposedGroups.reason: The target states that a business licensing by-law applies despite partial outside activity or no business place.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipal business licensing by-law applies even if the business is partly outside the municipality or has no place of business there.

reason: The section is a focused entitlement to a municipal trade licence without examination for certificate holders.

evidenceText: is entitled, upon payment of the prescribed fee, to be issued a licence without examination

proposedGroups.reason: The target covers apprenticeship and interprovincial certificate holders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a certificate holder is entitled to a municipal trade licence without examination after paying the prescribed fee.

reason: The section covers offences by licence holders for failing to produce a licence or breaking a condition.

evidenceText: Every holder of a licence issued under a by-law who

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies two licence-holder offences and category B punishment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offences for licence holders who fail to produce a licence without reasonable excuse or break a condition not otherwise punishable.

reason: The section is a focused provincial-licence prerequisite and municipal-licence statement rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Provincial licence prerequisite for municipal licence
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address provincial licence production and stating that fact on the municipal licence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a provincial licence must be produced before a municipal licence is valid and what the municipal licence must state.

reason: This target only applies the licence provisions in sections 112 to 116 to rural communities with necessary modifications.
The section authorizes specified municipal services to be undertaken as local improvements.

evidenceText: it may undertake the provision of such service as a local improvement under this part

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies sewerage, sidewalks, roads and streets, and water as local-improvement services.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which authorized services a municipality may undertake as local improvements.

reason: Section 118 is a long local-improvement definitions section; most terms group cleanly, but the tail work definition requires human review because the same-source context representation is truncated.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local improvement land and frontage terms
proposedGroups.reason: These terms define land, ownership, frontage measurement, and land value concepts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the local-improvement meanings of abutting parcel, frontage, metre frontage, owner, and value.

proposedGroups.reason: These terms distinguish municipal cost from the part specially assessed on owners.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meanings of municipality’s portion of the cost and owners’ portion of the cost.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local improvement works and systems terms
proposedGroups.reason: These terms define sewer, water, and work concepts used in local improvements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the local-improvement meanings of domestic sewer, sewerage works, surface sewer, and water system.

proposedGroups.reason: The target also defines work, but that tail definition needs human review because the same-source context representation is truncated.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the work definition for local improvements after human review of section 118.

reason: The section lists classes of local improvement work and allows combined classes as one work.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address work classes and combining two or more classes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the classes of work council may authorize as local improvements and that multiple classes may be undertaken as one work.

reason: Section 120 separates connections before paving or utility work, cost certification, and owner liability with recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Drain and water connections before paving
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize council resolutions directing connections and service work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council may direct drain connections, water service pipes, stop-cocks, and private drain connections before paving, sewer, or water main work.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern cost certification, evidentiary effect, and measurement from the street centre.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how connection and service-pipe costs are certified, what the certificate proves, and how the cost is measured.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Owner liability lien and recovery for installation
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections make costs payable by the owner, create a lien, and allow court recovery with interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when certified installation costs become payable, create a lien, and may be recovered from the owner with interest.

reason: The section defines what work cost is deemed to include.

evidenceText: The cost of a work is deemed to include

proposedGroups.reason: The target lists the cost components included in a work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what construction, engineering, surveying, compensation, debenture, interest, borrowing, and incidental expenses are included in the cost of a work.

reason: The section governs special frontage assessment work initiated by owner petition.

proposedGroups.reason: All subsections address petition support, thresholds, by-law vote, three-year timing, and partial work limits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a petition can support special frontage assessment work and the owner, value, council-vote, timing, and partial-work requirements.

reason: Section 123 separates the notice path for council-initiated work from the one-year restriction after opposition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice for council-initiated special frontage work
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address published notice, prescribed form, opposition threshold, two-thirds vote, and three-year authorization.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, opposition-petition, council-vote, and timing rules for council-initiated special frontage assessment work.

proposedGroups.reason: This subsection prohibits a second notice within one year after a sufficient opposition petition, subject to section 124.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the one-year limit on a second notice after a sufficient petition against proposed special frontage assessment work.
